verdict_reason: CORRECTED verdict (re-judged 2026-06-18). The PRIOR verdict scored pyMack against mack_ch10_fig10_1_M16_paper_complete.csv, which is NOT the Complete-Equations loop: it is an open, UPPER-branch-only trace with a non-physical low-R tail (extends to R~80 where no loop exists) and no nose/lower branch (see reference_data/digitized/mack_ch10_fig10_1_paper_complete_DEPRECATED_NOTE.md). Re-digitized Mack's INNERMOST (Complete-Equations) neutral LOOP from AGARD-R-709 p.90 with both branches + nose. Against that corrected loop, pyMack's first-mode neutral loop agrees to: lower(onset) branch median |dF|/F = 34%, upper(cutoff) branch 39% over 7 R in [400,1200]; loop-average 37% (worst branch 39%). At high R (R>=800), where Mack notes the M=1.6 curves converge, the agreement is better: lower 14% / upper 18%. Critical R: Mack ~215 vs pyMack ~400 (rel 86%); Mack nose F~1.75. pyMack's loop is WIDER/HIGHER than Mack's Complete loop -- its upper branch overlies the Dunn-Lin numerical/asymptotic loops rather than the Complete one -- the repo's documented low-Mach first-mode under-amplification / too-high critical Reynolds number. This is a real physics discrepancy, not the prior reference-curve error. DIGITIZATION-UNCERTAINTY CAVEAT: the 3 loops bundle at high R (Mack says they converge for R>700 at M=1.6), so branch F's carry ~5-12% reading error and the nose R is +/-20-25; even at the generous end of that uncertainty the M=1.6 critical-R gap and near-nose 2x width is robust. Verdict 'disagrees'.
